Welcome to the Team
SECTION A

Welcome to Snow School
Congratulations!  You have joined the biggest and most dynamic team at 
Horseshoe.
Here are few key things to remember as you navigate through training and 
orientation.
Mission
➔ At Horseshoe Resort Snow School, our mission is to elevate the resort’s 
reputation for excellence in outdoor sports instruction by delivering safe, 
high quality and engaging lessons-led by a team of skilled, passionate 
instructors 
➔ Our culture emphasizes safety, professionalism and continuous 
improvement-ensuring every instructor has the tools and support to lead 
with conﬁdence and consistency .
Expectations
➔ Be Punctual
➔ Be courteous to guests and fellow staff
➔ Provide excellent customer service to our guests
➔ Cell phones are to be used for work purposes only.  No picture 
taking/social media 
Duties and Responsibilities 
➔ Report for work on time and in uniform
➔ Scan in and out using ADP ﬁnger scanner/cell phone
➔ Check in with your supervisors for updates 
➔ Certiﬁed Instructors will lead groups/lessons
➔ Assistants will support and provide input to instructors in lesson/groups

Snow School Location & Info.
The Snow School ofﬁce and staff area  is downstairs in the Red Barn. We share 
this space with Lift and Outdoor operations. Please enter through the far door on 
the right side of the building (closest to the hill)
➔ The ADP scanner is located beside the fridge
➔ The right side of the room is for Snow School and Park staff. 
➔ The left side and round table is for the Lift Operators. 
➔ Staff info is on the table just outside the ofﬁce in the staff area i.e. 
stickers,progression cards, skills and drills or tool box handouts. You will 
also ﬁnd health and safety, session tracking sheets and any other info for 
the week will be posted here. 
➔ We have a kettle, microwave and fridge to share.  There are paper towels 
and cleaner for you to use should you make a mess.  Remember 
Kindergarten Rules - clean up after yourselves!
➔ Full time staff (4+ shifts/week) may store their skis/poles/boards in the staff 
storage area in the Red Barn.  All other equipment must go home at the 
end of your shift
➔ Be mindful of the space.  Store your things under table/chairs to leave 
room for others.
➔ Use appropriate language while in the Staff Room.  Again remember 
Kindergarten Rules: be kind and courteous.  
➔ The Staff Room is for staff only

Alpine Rentals, HV Sports Retail, Nordic Centre, and Snow School Teams. 
Snow School falls under the umbrella of the Recreation Team.  We are the largest 
department with the most staff.
All teams here at the resort are always working together to ensure the best experience 
possible for all of our guests!

Snow School Employee Pre-season Checklist
Congratulations and Welcome to Horseshoe Resort! We are excited about your 
ﬁrst day. You're joining a fantastic team and you will be a valued contributor. 
We’ve created a checklist below to help you complete your onboarding 
experience. These tasks are required to be completed before your ﬁrst day.
*EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT
❏ Sign your employment agreement
This has been emailed to you from our Human Resources team. It outlines our offer of 
employment to you.
*ADP - Our Scheduling and Payroll Application
❏ Create/Update your Proﬁle
❏ Add/Update Emergency Contacts
❏ Select Payment Option
❏ Review Documents
HSR Handbook, Hours of Work and Pay Information doc, Employee Perks document
❏ Upload Documents (VERY Important, see below)
Direct Deposit Information or Void Cheque. You must provide a bank authorized direct 
deposit form or a void cheque. Handwritten banking information will not be accepted.** 
If you do not upload this, we have no way of paying you!!!**
*FORMS - Employment and Training Availability and Contact Info
❏ Availability Form:
Click this link or type it into your browser to complete: 
https://forms.gle/2VE5xQH3fhhLWUYg6
This goes directly to your manager with your availability and contact info..
❏ Training Registration Form:
Click this link or type it into your browser to complete:

checklist. We look forward to having you on the team!

Standards & Expectations
Shift Standards
Expectations
➔ You are expected to be present in the Red Barn, dressed and ready for your shift at 
the start time on your scheduled day..
➔ Appropriate uniform means your Horseshoe issued Staff Jacket, black snow pants, 
helmet  and your snowboard/ski gear.
➔ Staff jackets are ONLY to be worn when you are WORKING.
➔ You will scan in and out for every shift at the ADP scanner located in the staff room, 
or on your cell phone when in the Red Barn. This will ensure your shift start and 
end times are recorded correctly.
Shift Rules
➔ Employees are entitled to a 30 minute break for every ﬁve and a half hours 
worked. You should not be leaving your work position to use your phone, grab a 
coffee, etc., at any other time unless approved by the team lead on duty, or 
manager (bathroom breaks excluded).
➔ If you are sent home less than three hours into your shift, you are entitled to three 
hours of pay.
➔ Do not borrow equipment from rentals.
➔ All equipment and environments must be set up prior to you riding/skiing for 
warm up.
➔ You are expected to be available should you be needed so do not hang out in 
other departments.  
➔ When your shift is over and all equipment is put away you may change out of 
your work jacket and enjoy the hill.
➔ No inversions in the Park or extreme riding while on shift and in uniform.
6

Shifts & Scheduling
Time-Off Requests & Scheduling
➔ You are expected to enter all time-off requests into ADP well in advance of 
schedule postings. Although we try to accommodate every time-off request that is 
submitted, requests are not guaranteed to be approved. If you have any concerns 
with your schedule, please speak with Administrative Supervisor or the Manager. 
➔ Time-off requests can be made in ADP under the “My Unavailability” section of 
scheduling viewing. 
➔ Schedules are posted in ADP. You can view your schedule or submit time-off 
requests on the ADP website or mobile app. 
Short Notice Shift Cancellation
➔ If you are not able to make your shift and you did not provide 2 weeks notice, you 
must:
◆ Inform your Manager  immediately
◆ Find a staff member to cover your shift. The replacement staff member 
must be of the same disciple as you.  Example: A ski Instructor cannot ask 
an assistant to cover their shift.
◆ Snow School management will help provide you contact numbers.
Scheduling Communications
➔ Any communication about shifts or scheduling must be made by the employee 
themselves.  For conﬁdentiality reasons, we will not disclose any shift or scheduling 
details to anyone who is not an employee of Horseshoe Resort.  
➔ Supervisors will provide all ofﬁce phone numbers and email addresses upon your 
ﬁrst shift.
Calling in Sick
➔ If you are feeling unwell and do not believe you should be at work as a result, 
please stay home for your shift. The health and well-being of you and the  team is 
our top priority. 
➔ If you must call in sick for your shift, please send an email to 
snowschool@horseshoeresort.com as soon as you are able to.  We will respond 
once received so that you know your cancellation is acknowledged.
Late Arrivals
➔ If you think you may be delayed in arriving to your shift, please send an email to 
snowschool@horseshoeresort.com Your safety is a priority, so please let us know if 
you are running late so that we don’t worry!

Guest and Resort Communication
SECTION C

Communication Standards
Representing the Resort
As a Snow School Team member you represent the ﬁrst and often most lasting 
impression for our guests. Your goal is to ensure each guest leaves with a positive and 
memorable experience.
Every member of the Snow School Team is a representative of the customer service at 
Horseshoe Resort. Your interaction with a guest can make or break their experience 
and their impression of Horseshoe Resort as a whole. 
What makes a good Customer Service Representative?
A good customer service REP is…
Resourceful
➔ Use your resources to ensure you are providing accurate and detailed 
information.
➔ If you don’t know the answer to a question, don’t be afraid to ask a team 
member for assistance, check the Horseshoe Resort website, direct the 
guest to another location, etc.
Empathetic
➔ Listen to your guests, make them feel welcome and heard. Remember 
that even just a smile goes a long way!
➔ No matter how many times you have heard a question, comment, or 
complaint in a day, it is the guest’s ﬁrst time interacting with you. 
Approach every interaction with patience and positivity. 
Proactive
➔ When assisting a guest, try to anticipate further questions they may 
have, and provide information they may not know they needed. 
➔ When you have a guest who may need a little extra assistance, take the 
initiative to provide the extra help! When the opportunity arises, always 
go above and beyond to improve a guest’s experience.

Guest & Resort Communication
Onsite Customer Service 
Every interaction you have with a guest of the resort reﬂects on you, the team, and the 
resort altogether. 
Greeting
➔ Always greet guests with a warm and welcoming smile. Remove Goggles so the 
guest can see your whole face.  Make eye contact.
➔ Acknowledge their presence promptly. Do not wait for them to acknowledge you. 
➔ Greet every passing guest, even when they are not coming to you directly. A quick 
“hello,” or “how are you today,” goes a long, long way. 
Presentation
➔ Ensure your uniform is always clean and presentable. Looking put-together drives 
a good impression of the team. 
Language
➔ Use clear, professional, and respectful language when speaking to a guest. 
➔ Avoid slang, use terms the guest will easily understand, and ensure 
communication is friendly but not overly casual. 
Radios
➔ Radios are used around the resort to communicate emergencies with Ski Patrol, 
and to reach other departments such as Lift Operations and Maintenance. 
➔ All Recreation Departments have a radio available at their shift stations. Snow 
School will give radios to each station during school groups and to the supervisors 
during programs.  
➔ A detailed list of radio channels, call numbers, and codes are kept at each radio 
charging station to use when needed. 
Calling Over the Radio
It is important to keep radio calls brief and to use proper language when 
communicating with other departments. 
25

Radio Etiquette
➔ Be mindful that everything you say can be heard by anyone on that channel and 
by anyone close by to a radio.
➔ Speak as clearly as possible. 
➔ If your department name is called over the radio (Guest Services, Rentals, etc), it is 
your responsibility to respond and assist. Do not wait for a manager to do it for you.

Private & Discovery Lessons
SECTION E

Private Lessons-Overview
Duration: 1 or 2 hours, 1-2 students
Expectations:
➔ Provide a fun and enjoyable skiing experience
➔ Safety is number one priority
➔ 2-3 teaching points in one lesson
Before Lesson Begins:
➔ Lesson booked at Guest Services.
➔ Meet outside of rentals at the  RED private lesson ﬂags. 
➔ Supervisor will greet the client and match them with an instructor.
Start of Lesson:
➔ Smile and introduce yourself.  Remove goggle so they see your face.  
Make eye contact.
➔ Try to connect quickly with the client, especially children. 
➔ Let the parent follow to the beginner area if they like, explain that you 
will drop the child off at the red ﬂags after the hour is over.
➔ Review Alpine Safety Code with client
Things to Consider Before Lesson Begins:
➔ Terrain choice - Know what the hill has to offer
➔ Demonstration - show what technique you are teaching
➔ Mileage: repetition of skill for skill competence
➔ Recap - be positive 
End of Lesson:
➔ Allow enough time to return to Red Flag 5 mins before end of the 
lesson.
➔ Review with client/parent what you worked & points for future 
progress.
➔ If parent is late for pick up, leave child with Supervisor and begin your 
next lesson.
➔ Thank them for coming and remind them they can request you in the 
future.

Discovery Lessons-Overview
Duration: 120 minutes for 10-15 students, 60 minutes for 5 or less students
Saturdays and Sundays
Details:
➔ New skiers/boarders
➔ Rentals and lift passes included in package
➔ Clients will receive neck buffs
Expectations:
➔ Provide a fun and enjoyable ﬁrst time skiing experience
➔ Quick progression is not the priority, fun is.
Before Lesson Begins:
➔ Lesson is  booked at Guest Services.
➔ Meet outside of rentals at the  Discover Lesson ﬂags. 
➔ Assist with equipment and RFID cards
Start of Lesson:
➔ Smile and introduce yourself. Remove goggles so they see your face.  
Make eye contact.
➔ Ensure clients have proper outerwear and helmets and that they are 
worn properly.  
➔ Check that equipment ﬁts and is on properly
➔ Review Alpine Safety Code with clients
During Lesson:
➔ Review equipment and demonstrate taking it on and off
➔ Practice on one ski different locomotion.  Add second ski
➔ Practice falling and getting up.
➔ Explain carpet safety
➔ Ensure clients are able to successfully stop before they go on carpet.
➔ Be positive in encouragement and feedback
End of Lesson:
➔ Thank clients for choosing Horseshoe.
➔ Offer private lessons and remind then they can request you.

Beginner Ski Lesson                                                 
  (ages 3-99) 
Beginning of First Lesson 
➔ Make eye contact, smile and introduce yourself.
➔ Learn names of skiers, and number of skiers in your group. 
➔ Show skiers something unique to remember who you are. 
➔ If children, give stickers, make a connection with as many as you can
➔ Discuss a meeting place if they get separated, ﬂags, chalet door outside, 
bottom of carpet..etc
➔ Reassure them that you will come back for them if they get separated, tell 
them to stay where they last saw you.
 
Stage #1: Flatland Mobility
10-15mins
Flats in front of rentals
➔ Learning the ﬂats, with cones, snow paint etc( stance and balance, safety, 
location of hills etc) 
➔ We have set up 2-3 squares with ski poles and cones 
➔ Ask each student to show: 
◆ A ski stance in boots 
● How to push their leg to the side in boots
● A relaxed pizza stance 
● Weight on toes and turn heels out or push heels out in boots
● Explain ski equipment show how to take on and off 
● Ask everyone to put on right ski and walk around poles pushing heel out 
at each ski pole 
● Switch skis go opposite direction 
● Once conﬁdent put 2 skis on try walking in a square 
● Lineup try pushing skis out to pizza balanced stance weight on toes 
● If they can do that they can move on to station 2

Stage #2: Gliding
30 min.  
Small carpet
➔ Teach carpet safety
➔ Each student should have a chance to sidestep up a hill and do a few glides before 
using the little carpet, this is done to the left of the carpet. 
➔ Students will stay at at small carpet until they can stop on command ( stance and 
balance while gliding, mobility and edges on traverse) 
➔  Explain alpine code 1&2
➔ Demonstrate how to get up after a fall, practice
➔ Gliding to a stop on a gentle run with no obstacles at the bottom 
➔ Add some cones for visual stop areas 
Stage #3:  Speed Control
30 min or more
Kimble Carpet
➔ Teach carpet safety
➔ Top of big carpet to mid way on hill 
➔ Works on speed control and stopping 
➔ Add foam characters, cones and character signs for visual stopping locations OR 
snow paint, should be easily moved or very soft.
Stage #4:   Direction Change
30 min
Top of Kimble
➔ Starts to learn turning 
➔ Developing conﬁdence 
➔ Maximum speed on minimum terrain
➔ Add brushies 
➔ Foam stubbies 
➔ Snow paint for making tracks to follow 
Stage 5: Chair safety and use 
5 min.    
Model chair at top of chair 1 
➔ Give instruction on how to load and unload have everyone try 
Beginner Ski Lesson, con’t

Beginner Snowboard Lesson                                                 
  (ages 3-99) 
Beginning of First Lesson 
➔ Make eye contact, smile and introduce yourself.
➔ Learn names of skiers, and number of skiers in your group. 
➔ Show skiers something unique to remember who you are. 
➔ If children, give stickers, make a connection with as many as you can
➔ Discuss a meeting place if they get separated, ﬂags, chalet door outside, bottom of 
carpet..etc
➔ Reassure them that you will come back for them if they get separated, tell them to 
stay where they last saw you.
 
Stage #1: Flatland Basics
10-15mins
Flats in front of rentals
Part A
➔ Check:
◆ Helmet on and buckled Gloves, RFID and lift ticket,boots tied correctly
➔ Explain
◆ Bindings, toe, tail,edges
◆ How to open and close bindings (foot in foot out) 
➔ Standing in neutral position, back straight, knees bent eyes up 
➔ Zipper straight up and down head up eyes forward 
➔ Shift weigh over one foot ( hip over foot ) switch to other foot 
➔ Back straight, knees bent,eyes forward
➔ Rock back and forth between heels and toes 
Part B
➔ Sliding on one foot 
➔ Putting board on and off 
➔ Alpine code 1&2
➔ Location of various lifts 
➔ How to ﬁnd a neutral position
Part C
➔ Place back foot behind board spin board on the ground ( do the twist )
➔ Back to neutral position( knees back eyes)
➔ Lift board horizontal ( checking for boots and binding tight enough at the same 
time as feeling the weight of the board )
➔  Back to neutral 
➔ Lift toe, slide the board side to side on the spot 
➔ Try to push the board away from body while on heel edge, explain this is the brake 
➔ Step free foot over board, bend knee, now heel edge lifts. take a few steps forward, 
this is how we walk up hill
➔ One foot back hand cross in front of chest pivot around/switch other direction 
➔ Slides in both directions

Stage #2: Sliding and Control
30-40 min.  
Small carpet
➔ Sliding with one foot in 
➔ Control with sideslipping 
➔ Attaching a board on slopeside 
➔ Two feet attached 
➔ Walk up hill, back straight,knees bent, eyes up 
➔ Slide down hill toe drag into j turn complete 1-3 slides 
➔ Strap in both feet once student shows competency with one

Teaching Children
SECTION G

Working with Children - Things to Consider
Know your learner: 
➔ Getting to know your learner and building rapport is a vital step in 
creating an enjoyable lesson. 
➔ Learner based approach guides all the decisions we make as instructors.
Be Prepared: 
➔ Bring with you to the lesson: pens, class cards, tissues, stickers, cry 
stoppers hand warmers,, ect.
➔ Have games ready to play while waiting for your students to arrive
Introductions: 
➔ Introduce yourself to the students, and them to each other
➔ Add things that may help students bond. Eg. this is Sam’s ﬁrst day too, he 
has a dog who else has a dog?
➔ Make it a point to know their names.
➔ Make sure they know who you are and how to identify you.
Important Points: 
★ We have a duty of care to any minor.  You are legally responsible for 
them while they are in a lesson and until they are back in the care of 
the parent/guardian.
➔ We do not tolerate a child who is physical or using inappropriate 
language with anyone.
➔ If at any time you have a child who is not able to keep up with the group, 
let a supervisor know.
➔ Do not talk about a child’s development in front of them. Step aside to 
talk to the supervisor when they are out of ear shot. Careful what you say 
in front of them.
➔ Many children are VERY young and this is new and scary experience. Be 
mindful/sensitive of their feelings. If they’re having a tough time call your 
supervisor.
➔ We do not yell at children. We model the behaviour we want to see.  
➔ Children respond best to positivity and words of afﬁrmations. Let’s 
remember to tell the child what they’re doing well. “Wow Johny I can see 
you are working really hard on getting your toe edge”.

Working with Children - Things to Consider, con’t
Lesson Management:
➔ Count your students all the time.  You must know how many are in your 
group at all times.
➔ To avoid losing a child do the following:
◆ Arrange a meeting spot with your group prior to the start of the 
lesson.
◆ Give clear, concise directions.  Repeat them and be sure everyone 
has heard them.  Have them repeat them back to you.
◆ Instructors and Assistants are a team.  One will lead the group 
down the run and the other will be at the back of the group.  This  
hold true for using the  chairlifts.
➔ IF YOU HAVE LOST A STUDENT
◆ Remain Calm
◆ Call your Supervisor immediately
◆ Either the Instructor or Assistant stays with the group and the other 
check meeting spot.
◆ On the radio the code is ORANGE
◆ Be sure you know the students name and what they are wearing
➔ IF THERE IS AN INJURY
◆ Call your Supervisor and call ski patrol
◆ Be sure to tell them where you are located
◆ Do not move the student
◆ At the time of the incident move your other students to a safe place 
on the side of the hill. 
◆ Mark the incident with crossed skis or your snowboard to have 
some visual aid for other people not to run into you. 
◆ STAY CALM
◆ When Patrol arrives give them all the information you can about 
the accident.
◆ If needed, a supervisor will stay with the injured party so you carry 
on with the the lesson
◆ You may have to ﬁll out an incident report afterwards.

Lift Safety
SECTION H

Lift Safety
Chairlift:  First Time Users
➔ Stand off to the side of the lift and have students watch others getting on 
chairlift.
➔ Note the following steps:
◆ Wait at ﬁrst line
◆ Wait for the chair to come in front of you
◆ Shufﬂe after the chair to the next line
◆ Look behind and sit when chair comes around.
◆ Pull bar down.
◆ Ride the chair sitting face forward
➔ While on the lift remind students to stay facing forward and discuss how 
to disembark.  Ask if anyone needs help.
➔ Instructor should be last off the lift
➔ If a student falls getting off the lift or does not disembark, do not try and 
catch them/push them off.  The lift operator will stop the lift and assist 
you.
➔ Use the Practice Chair at the top of Kimble carpet.  Practice getting on 
and off so the students get comfortable.
➔ For students to ride solo (or with Peers) they must:
◆ Pass the safety lesson and get a safety sticker for helmet.  3rd week 
of lessons minimum.
◆ Be at least 6 years  old and 45” tall 
◆ Embark/disembark and raise/lower the safety bar unassisted
◆ Read/understand Resort map
◆ Recall safe meeting spot for group
Carpet:  First Time Users
➔ Ask questions and walk them through the process. Don’t assume they 
know how.
➔ All staff must be wearing equipment on the large carpet ( Kimble)
➔ Show your students the posted signs on the lift.  Explain their meaning.
➔ Explain what will happen at the top of the hill.
➔ Keep the least experienced student closest to you so you can help if 
needed.
➔ The ﬁrst few times you can load the student and walk up beside them so 
you’re there to help unload. (Small carpet only) 
➔ Remind them of what to do leading up to the carpet and throughout the 
process. Bend your knees, don’t walk on the carpet etc.
